title: Divine Kerala: A 5 Night Kerala Couple Tour Package
summary: A 5 night 6 day kerala couple tour package through Munnar, Thekkady, an Alleppey houseboat and Varkala, with stays, transfers and sightseeing arranged.
body_markdown:
Few trips change scenery as often as this one. In six days you move from tea covered hills to a spice plantation, from a houseboat on still backwaters to a clifftop above the Arabian Sea. That range, packed into a single unhurried route, is what makes Kerala such a natural choice for couples who want variety without constant repacking and replanning.


## **What This Curated Kerala Trip Sets Out to Do**


This is the Divine Kerala trip, a kerala couple tour package built around five distinct stops rather than one base. It moves from Munnar to Thekkady to Alleppey and on to Varkala, giving each landscape a proper stretch of time instead of a rushed half day.


Every stay, transfer and sightseeing stop inside Kerala is arranged as one plan, so the trip stays restful. You can look at the current couple options and start an enquiry on the[Chyll by zing packages page](https://www.zingbus.com/tour-packages) , with the full details and booking held on the zingbus app.


# **Divine Kerala: A Complete Kerala Couple Tour Package for Six Days**


This is a 5 night, 6 day route that begins and ends at Kochi. It is a curated Chyll by zing trip rather than a bus journey, so you reach Kochi by your own flight or train, and everything from there, the cabs, the stays, the guide and the sightseeing, is handled for you. Here is how the six days unfold, stop by stop, along with the properties, what is covered and the practical details.


## **What Makes Kerala a Couples Trip**


Kerala works for two people because the days ask very little of you. The distances between stops are short enough to drive in a morning, which leaves afternoons free for a tea garden walk, a slow cruise or an evening on a cliff. The pace is the appeal, not the mileage.


The variety helps too. A honeymoon or a quiet couple trip does not have to mean one resort for a week. This route gives you hill country, a wildlife park, a spice plantation, a backwater night and a beach town in one loop, so the mood shifts every day or two without you ever having to organise the switch.


## **The Six Day Route at a Glance**


The table below lays out the shape of the trip so you can see how the nights are split before reading the detail. Each stop has its own character, and the order is built so the landscape changes gradually rather than all at once.


**Stage** **Where** **Nights**


Day 1 to 2 Munnar, tea hills 2


Day 3 Thekkady, spice country 1


Day 4 Alleppey, houseboat 1


Day 5 Varkala, coast 1


Day 6 Return to Kochi Departure


## **Munnar: Tea Country and Eravikulam**


The trip opens with the drive from Kochi up to Munnar, breaking at the Cheeyappara and Valara waterfalls on the way. The first evening is a sunset walk through the tea gardens, which is the gentlest possible start to a couple’s trip. Two nights here give the hills room to breathe.


The full Munnar day takes place in Eravikulam National Park, home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr, along with the Tea Museum, Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point and a quiet afternoon by Kundala Lake. Munnar sits high enough that mornings are cool, so the tea country here feels distinct from the coast you reach later.


## **Thekkady: Spice Country and the Periyar Cruise**


From Munnar the route drops to Thekkady, where the landscape turns to cardamom, pepper and other spices. A plantation walk explains what actually grows here, and the afternoon brings the scenic boat ride on Periyar Lake, which is one of the experiences built into the plan rather than an optional add on.


The evening often includes a traditional Kathakali or Kalaripayattu performance, both rooted in Kerala rather than staged for tourists elsewhere. Thekkady is a single night, which is enough to see the plantation and the lake before the route moves toward the water.


## **Alleppey: A Night on the Backwaters**


Day four is the one most people picture when they think of Kerala. You board a traditional houseboat at Alleppey and spend the day cruising the backwaters, with lunch served onboard as the water and paddy fields slide past. Sunset and dinner happen on the boat, and you sleep on the water.


This is the trip’s centrepiece, and it earns the billing. One practical note applies: houseboat check in is subject to availability, so the exact boat is confirmed close to the date rather than fixed far in advance.


## **Varkala: Clifftops and the Arabian Sea**


The final stretch runs to Varkala, with a stop at the Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple, known for its Pal Payasam, and the Jatayu Earth Centre on the way. Varkala itself is a cliff town above the Arabian Sea, and the evening on the North Cliff, with its cafe strip at sunset, is a fitting close to the route.


The last morning is deliberately slow: the quieter South Cliff or an Ayurveda session, then a late checkout and the drive back to Kochi with lunch on the way, reaching the airport or railway station by evening. It ends the trip on the coast rather than back in the hills, which suits the arc of the six days.


## **Where You Stay**


The properties are named across the route and span comfortable to genuinely lovely. In Munnar the stays are Valley View, rated 4.6, and Grand Plaza Munnar, also 4.6. Thekkady is Spices Lap Resort at 4.7, Alleppey is the Waves and Dales houseboat at 4.7, and Varkala is Urban Cliff at 4.9, which is the highest rated stay across the whole Chyll range.


One caveat applies to all of them. The final stay is allocated based on availability, at one of the listed properties or a similarly rated property in the same area with comparable amenities. Early check in, where you want it, is also subject to availability, which is worth keeping in mind on the days with a morning arrival.


## **What the Package Covers and What It Does Not**


This is where accuracy matters most. The trip includes all local transfers in partnered cabs across Kerala, a trip guide throughout, the accommodation, the scenic boat ride on Periyar Lake, and the sightseeing set out in the itinerary. Notably, there is no intercity bus leg on this trip. It begins and ends at Kochi, which you reach by your own flight or train, and the arranged portion is everything inside Kerala.


The standard exclusions apply. These cover the 5% GST, any extra food, snacks, tea, coffee or beverages beyond the meals mentioned, anything not specifically listed in the inclusions, and any added cost from unforeseen situations such as weather, roadblocks, landslides or heavy rains. On cancellations, more than 15 days before departure is a full refund, 7 to 15 days is a 50% refund, and within 7 days is non refundable.


## **How to Plan and Book**


Package pricing for this kerala couple tour package is not published here, and the current fare sits with the live listing rather than a blog. The practical step is to open the zingbus app, where the full couple range and the booking flow live, since not every option appears on the website. Carry a valid government photo ID for the trip, as stays and travel will ask for it.


If the fixed route does not match your dates or how long you want in each place, the custom trip enquiry lets you shape it. You can start that from the same Chyll by zing planner, choosing the destination, the vibe and the stay style, and the rest is worked out from there. For couples reaching Kochi by air, timing the flights around a morning arrival on day one makes the first drive to Munnar easier.


## **Why This Route Suits a Slow Couple Trip**


The strength of this kerala couple tour package is that it never feels like a checklist, even though it covers a lot of ground. Each stop gets enough time to settle in before the next, and the order moves you gently from the hills to the coast rather than bouncing around the map. For a honeymoon or an anniversary, that steady rhythm matters more than squeezing in extra sights.


If it appeals, plan the Kochi arrival first, keep the packing light since you change base four times, and let the arranged transfers carry the logistics. What you are left with is the part that matters: tea gardens, a spice trail, a night on the backwaters and a last evening above the sea.


## **Planning Your Kerala Couple Trip: Common Questions**


These are the questions couples tend to ask before booking this route, answered briefly.


### **What does this Kerala couple tour package include?**


This kerala couple tour package includes all local cab transfers in Kerala, a trip guide, the stays, the Periyar Lake boat ride and the sightseeing in the itinerary. There is no bus leg.


### **How long is the Divine Kerala trip?**


The Divine Kerala trip runs for 5 nights and 6 days, starting and ending at Kochi, and moving through Munnar, Thekkady, an Alleppey houseboat and Varkala along the way.


### **Does the package include a bus from my city to Kerala?**


No, this trip has no intercity bus leg. It begins and ends at Kochi, which you reach by your own flight or train, and everything inside Kerala is arranged for you.


### **Is this trip suitable for a honeymoon?**


Yes, the route suits a honeymoon well. The slow pace, the houseboat night, the tea hills and the clifftop evenings in Varkala give it a naturally romantic character across the six days.


### **Which places does the Divine Kerala route cover?**


The route covers Munnar for two nights, then Thekkady, an Alleppey houseboat and Varkala for one night each, before returning to Kochi on the final day for departure.


### **Is the houseboat stay guaranteed?**


The houseboat night at Alleppey is part of the plan, though check in is subject to availability, so the exact boat is confirmed nearer the travel date rather than fixed far ahead.


### **What is the best time to visit Kerala for this trip?**


The clear, post monsoon months from roughly October to March are the most comfortable for this route, with pleasant hill mornings in Munnar and calmer coastal evenings in Varkala.


### **What kind of stays are included?**


The stays range from comfortable hill properties in Munnar to a 4.7 rated houseboat in Alleppey and a 4.9 rated clifftop stay in Varkala, allocated based on availability.


### **Do we need to trek on this trip?**


There is no hard trek on this route. Expect easy walking at Eravikulam National Park, through tea gardens and along the Varkala cliffs, all at a relaxed pace rather than a strenuous one.


### **How do we book or customise this trip?**


Booking and the full couple range sit on the zingbus app. For different dates or more time in one place, use the custom trip enquiry on the Chyll by zing planner.


### **Is the trip good for first time visitors to Kerala?**


Yes, this route is a strong first visit, since it covers the hills, a spice region, the backwaters and the coast in one loop, giving a full sense of the state in under a week.


### **What should couples pack for this trip?**


Pack light since you change base four times, and bring a mix of cool cottons for the coast, a light layer for Munnar’s cool mornings, comfortable walking shoes and a valid government photo ID.
